newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania says to avoid inflation in pyramid payback.
newsitem.headline: Albania says to avoid inflation in pyramid payback.

text.p: Albanian Finance Minister Ridvan Bode said on Friday he would seek to keep a lid on inflation by encouraging investors in failed pyramid schemes to accept bank certificates, rather than hard cash, as compensation.
Albania's right-wing government has promised partial compensation to investors who plunged money into two failed pyramid investment funds, beginning February 5.

"To minimise the risk of inflation, there should be a national understanding with as few people as possible claiming to withdraw their deposits in cash immediately," Bode told Albanian television in an interview.
Inflation was 17.4 percent year-on-year in 1996,and economists have warned that the pyramid scandal could spark hyper-inflation in the impoverished European country.
"We are taking every precaution to make sure that this process is overcome with the least possible inflationary pressure...because many other problems could arise from inflation," Bode said.

The government has frozen some $300 million of funds held in state banks by the two failed pyramid schemes. Bode said all other assets owned by the schemes would be auctioned to raise money for out-of-pocket investors.
In the wake of the crisis, the Albanian lek has dropped some 30 percent against the dollar since the start of the year.
Bode said the lek's fall was not caused by macro-economic reasons.

"What is actually happening in the market nowadays is a simple psychological effect, which has nothing to do with...the economy," Bode said. "The bid/ask ratio does not reflect the real exchange rate between the lek and the dollar."
